close_reason: upload_blob now cross-checks BlobUploadResponse.size against actual data.len() before returning. Mismatch surfaces as UnexpectedResponse with both sizes in the message. Used UnexpectedResponse rather than adding a typed variant to keep 0.1.x API stable; typed BlobSizeMismatch can be added in 0.2.0. New regression test pins the contract.
description: src/blob.rs:213-241 — after upload, the client deserializes BlobUploadResponse and verifies the server's sha256 (when present) but never checks that `upload_resp.size == data.len() as u64`. A buggy server reporting size=0 with a valid sha256 would be accepted. Low-severity: the sha256 check, when present, makes a size mismatch implausible (length is implicit in the digest). When sha256 is absent (most servers), size is the only signal of "the bytes I sent are the bytes you received" — silently ignoring it gives up that signal. Optional: assert size match and return BlobIntegrityMismatch on disagreement.
title: BlobUploadResponse.size returned by server is never validated against actually-uploaded byte count
